name: Zedoary Wash
lede: Zedoary wash is a warm, golden yellow named after a turmeric relative; the name goes back to Robert Dossie in 1764.

sections.title: A yellow from a root
sections.body:
The Pigment Compendium records "zedoary wash" as a name used by Robert Dossie in 1764 [1]. It would come from *Curcuma zedoaria*, a plant of north-east India related to turmeric [1]. The entry adds that Dossie may not have told zedoary from turmeric, so the source could really be turmeric [1]. The preparation was boiling the root in water [1].

As a color word the name is much newer, recorded by Maerz and Paul in 1930 as a plate 10 yellow, with a first record year of 1764 [2]. The swatch is a moderate orange yellow, about 4.4 units from the ISCC-NBS name [2].

sections.title: In paintings
sections.body: A yellow near this swatch is common in the archive: 528 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed [3]. It peaks in the 1300s, at 3.5 times the baseline, and the most devoted painter is George Dawe, in 13 of 50 works [3]. These are look-alike hues in photographs, not evidence of zedoary [3].

questions.q: Zedoary is a relative of which plant?
True or false: Dossie certainly meant zedoary, not turmeric.

openers: Zedoary wash dates to 1764, and it may secretly be turmeric.
